h1: The 7 Best Air Fryer Toaster Ovens for Real Weeknight Cooking, Ranked & Reviewed
metaTitle: Best Air Fryer Toaster Ovens: Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: 7 air fryer toaster ovens scored on capacity, wattage, presets, footprint and versatility, from Breville to budget picks.
summary: The Breville Smart Oven Air Fryer Pro is the one to buy if you want presets and faster, more even cooking from a single countertop oven. The Cuisinart 8-in-1 1800W is the best value for a family that wants one oven for most meals, the Emeril Lagasse 26 Quart is the pick for big batches, and the BLACK+DECKER 4-slice is the simple, low-cost way to get air frying on the counter.
intro: Most people shop for an air fryer toaster oven by counting functions. Eight modes, nine modes, twelve modes. The number is almost meaningless, because on every one of these ovens the same few elements and the same fan do all the work. What changes your dinners is the physical stuff: how much usable cavity you have, how much wattage feeds the heat, and whether the oven can run an air fry cycle without turning the kitchen into a sauna.

This ranking sorts seven air fryer toaster ovens by how well each one covers the full job of a countertop oven: air frying, baking, broiling and toasting. We reviewed the manufacturer specifications and listings for wattage, capacity, controls and design, and we say so plainly when a listing leaves a detail out, rather than guessing at numbers we cannot verify.

products.name: Breville BOV900BSS Smart Oven Air Fryer Pro
products.verdict: The most capable countertop oven here, with presets, brushed stainless steel construction and faster cooking.
products.description:
The Breville BOV900BSS Smart Oven Air Fryer Pro is a brushed stainless steel countertop oven built around a smart preset system. It is the model here aimed at cooks who want the oven to manage the heat rather than manage it themselves.

It takes first place because the Breville design philosophy is about control over a long list of cooking modes, not just a list of icons. Presets set time and temperature for common foods, and the faster cooking approach reduces the wait you accept from a countertop oven. Against the Cuisinart models behind it, the Breville gives up the lower price and the simplicity of a dial and gives you a more polished, more adjustable machine that suits anyone who bakes and roasts often.

It is the right oven for a serious home cook and a poor one for someone who just wants to reheat pizza, because the premium shows in the price bucket. Check that it fits your counter and the cabinet above it before ordering, as the Breville is a large appliance.
products.idealFor: Serious home cooks who want one countertop oven that does it all with presets.
products.skipIf: You only reheat and toast and do not want to pay for presets.

products.name: Cuisinart 8-in-1 Air Fryer Toaster Oven, 1800W
products.verdict: An 1800W convection oven with eight functions that covers most family meals for less than the Breville.
products.description:
The Cuisinart 8-in-1 combines an 1800 watt heating system with eight functions: air fry, convection, bake, broil and warm among them. It sits in the $100 to $200 bucket and is the more affordable of the two Cuisinart ovens on this list.

It ranks second because it hits the sweet spot of power and price. Eighteen hundred watts is the practical ceiling for a 15 amp household circuit, so the oven can heat quickly and recover after you open the door, and convection fans move that heat around the food. Compared with the Breville, you lose the presets and the finer control, but you keep nearly all the real cooking range at a lower cost. Against the Cuisinart with Grill, you skip a grill function you may never use.

It is the best choice for a family that wants one appliance to do most dinners. The caveat is the usual one for a convection oven: air frying works best with a single layer, so a big batch of wings still needs two rounds.
products.idealFor: Families who want one oven for most weeknight meals at a sensible price.
products.skipIf: You want presets or the finest temperature control.

products.name: Emeril Lagasse 26 Quart French Door Air Fryer Oven
products.verdict: A 26 quart cavity with French doors for family-sized batches.
products.description:
The Emeril Lagasse oven has a 26 quart capacity and a French door design, where the two doors open outward together. It sits in the $100 to $200 bucket and targets larger meals and family batches.

It ranks third because capacity is its defining trait. Twenty-six quarts is a lot of cavity, which gives you room for a whole chicken, a full sheet of cookies or a pizza that would crowd a smaller oven. French doors make loading easier at the front of the counter, since two narrow doors swing less space than one big drop-down door. The tradeoff against the Cuisinart is size and weight, because a bigger cavity takes up more counter, and more air to heat means longer preheat than a compact model.

It is the right choice for a household of four or more that cooks full meals in the oven. If you have a small kitchen, a compact oven is a better use of space.
cons: Needs a lot of counter space
products.idealFor: Households of four or more that cook whole meals in a countertop oven.
products.skipIf: Your counter is small or you cook for one or two.

products.name: Cuisinart Air Fryer Toaster Oven with Grill, 1800W
products.verdict: The same 1800W platform with convection bake, a grill option and broil and warm settings.
products.description:
This Cuisinart is an 1800 watt, eight-function oven that adds a grill option to bake, convection bake, broil and warm. It sits in the $200 to $500 bucket, one step above the 8-in-1 model.

It ranks fourth because the grill is the only meaningful difference from the cheaper Cuisinart, and the price bucket is higher. If you like searing steaks, burgers or sandwiches with a charred top, the grill mode does that job in a countertop oven without a pan on the stove. For everyone else, the 8-in-1 delivers the same power at a lower price, which is why this one ranks below it in value.

Buy it if the grill function is something you will actually use weekly. Skip it if you mostly air fry and bake, because you will be paying for a mode that sits unused.
cons: Grill mode suits a narrow use
products.idealFor: Cooks who want a grill setting and an air fryer in one oven.
products.skipIf: You will not use the grill and would rather keep the savings.

products.name: Ninja Flip Toaster Oven and Air Fryer SP151
products.verdict: An 8-in-1 stainless steel Ninja designed to save counter space.
products.description:
The Ninja Flip SP151 is an 8-in-1 stainless steel toaster oven and air fryer. It is aimed at small kitchens with limited counter space, which is the reason to look at it ahead of the larger ovens here.

It ranks fifth because it trades capacity for footprint. A compact oven means less cavity, so it handles toast, small sheet pans and personal pizzas better than a family roast. Eight functions give it the same basic range as the Cuisinart 8-in-1, though the listing does not give a wattage or a cavity size, so we cannot compare heating power directly. Ninja's name is a reasonable signal for build and support, and the stainless finish wipes clean easily.

Counter space is the deciding factor here, and the oven suits a cook feeding one or two people. If you cook for a family, the Emeril or the Cuisinart is a better use of a counter.
products.idealFor: One or two people in a small kitchen who want air frying and toasting.
products.skipIf: You cook family-sized meals and need a large cavity.

products.name: Our Place Wonder Oven 6-in-1 Air Fryer Toaster Oven
products.verdict: A 13 quart, two-rack design-forward oven that adds steam and speed to the usual air fry modes.
products.description:
The Our Place Wonder Oven is a 6-in-1 air fryer and toaster oven with a 13 quart capacity and a two-rack interior. It appeals to design-minded cooks who like steam and speed in a small, good-looking appliance.

It ranks sixth because 13 quarts is a compact cavity and six functions is the shortest list of the group. The appeal is style and the steam-assisted approach, which helps with reheating bread and keeping some foods moist. Two racks let you cook on two levels, which is handy for a side and a main in one go, but a small cavity limits the size of each piece. Against the Ninja Flip, it is similar in size and trades a function or two for a more distinctive look.

It makes sense for a small household that cares about how the appliance looks on the counter. If you want the most cooking for the money, look at the Cuisinart.
products.idealFor: Small households that want a good-looking oven with steam features.
products.skipIf: You want a large cavity or the best value per function.

products.name: BLACK+DECKER 4-Slice 5-in-1 Air Fry Toaster Oven
products.verdict: A simple, low-cost 4-slice oven that adds air frying to the basics.
products.description:
The BLACK+DECKER is a 4-slice, 5-in-1 countertop oven with an air fry function. It is the lowest-cost model here, in the $50 to $100 bucket, and targets simple everyday cooking.

It ranks last not because it is poor but because it is the most basic. A 4-slice cavity fits toast, a small tray of fries or a few chicken pieces, and five functions cover toast, bake, broil, air fry and warm. The listing does not give a wattage or a preset system, so we treat it as a no-frills entry model. Against the Ninja Flip, you get a lower price and a simpler oven at the cost of a smaller range of functions.

It suits a dorm, a first apartment or a second kitchen where you want air frying without a big spend. Do not expect it to replace a full oven for family meals.
pros: Adds air frying to a toaster
products.idealFor: Dorms, first apartments and second kitchens on a tight budget.
products.skipIf: You cook for a family or want presets.

methodology.title: Cooking range
methodology.description: We looked at how many real modes each oven offers, including air fry, convection bake, broil, warm and extras such as grill or steam, and discounted modes that duplicate each other.

methodology.title: Power and heat
methodology.description: Wattage and convection design determine preheat time and how well heat holds after the door opens. We favored 1800W ovens and flagged listings that omit wattage.

methodology.title: Capacity and footprint
methodology.description: Cavity size sets what you can cook, and counter size sets whether the oven earns its place. We balanced both rather than rewarding the largest unit.

methodology.title: Controls and presets
methodology.description: Smart presets, dials and simple buttons all trade off flexibility against ease of use. We scored for the control style that suits the oven's target buyer.

methodology.title: Price and value
methodology.description: We compared the price bucket against what you get, so a mid-priced oven with strong power ranked above a premium model that adds little for the same job.

whatMatters.detail: Wattage is the heating power, and on a 15 amp household circuit about 1800 watts is the practical maximum for a plug-in oven. More watts mean faster preheat and quicker recovery after you open the door. Look for the wattage on the listing, because a missing figure often means a lower-powered unit.

Capacity is quoted in quarts or slices, but what matters is what fits: a 9 by 13 inch pan, a 12 inch pizza or a whole chicken. A bigger cavity cooks more at once but needs more counter and more preheat time. Match the cavity to your largest regular dish and your household size.

Air frying is convection with a stronger fan and a high, dry heat. In a toaster oven, performance depends on how well the fan moves air around the food and how much of the cavity you can use in a single layer. Check whether the listing separates air fry from convection bake, and expect to cook in a single layer.

Dials are quick and durable, while digital panels and presets add precision and convenience. A preset is only useful if you cook the foods it covers, so read the preset list. Premium ovens like the Breville justify the price here by controlling the heat for you.

A countertop oven throws heat from the top and sides, so it needs clear space above and around it. Measure the counter, the cabinet above and the cord reach before you buy. A compact oven or a flip-up design can be the difference between using it daily and burying it in a cabinet.

cards.label: Presets
cards.text: The oven picks time and temperature for common foods and manages the heat. Easier and more consistent, but pricier. Pick: Breville BOV900BSS.

cards.label: Manual dials and buttons
cards.text: You set time and temperature yourself. Cheaper and fast to learn, with more room for your own judgment. Picks: Cuisinart 8-in-1, Cuisinart with Grill, Emeril Lagasse, BLACK+DECKER.

howToChoose.note: Default to manual control unless you bake often and want the oven to manage it for you.

cards.label: Look for
cards.text: High wattage, a stated air fry mode separate from convection, and a cavity wide enough to spread food in a single layer. A rack and tray that allow airflow underneath also help.

cards.label: In this ranking
cards.text: Cuisinart 8-in-1 for the best balance, Breville BOV900BSS for presets, and Emeril Lagasse for big batches. The Our Place Wonder Oven suits small loads.

cards.label: Spend more if
cards.text: You bake, roast and cook daily and want the oven to manage the heat. The Breville BOV900BSS or the Cuisinart with Grill justifies the step up.

cards.label: Save if
cards.text: You mostly toast, reheat and air fry a few snacks. The BLACK+DECKER or the Ninja Flip does the job.

faq.q: Will an air fryer toaster oven fit under my cabinets?
faq.a: Measure first, because these ovens vary a lot in height and depth and they need clear space above for heat. The Emeril Lagasse 26 quart and the Breville are the largest here, while the Ninja Flip and BLACK+DECKER are designed to take less room.

faq.q: What is the most common mistake with these ovens?
faq.a: Overloading the tray so air cannot circulate. Spread food in a single layer for crisp results and cook in two rounds if needed, which matters most on smaller cavities like the Our Place Wonder Oven.

faq.q: Is a Breville worth it over a Cuisinart?
faq.a: If you bake and roast often and like presets, yes. The Cuisinart 8-in-1 has the same 1800W class of power at a lower cost and covers most meals, so for simple weeknight cooking the extra money buys convenience more than capability.

faq.q: Do I need to preheat an air fryer toaster oven?
faq.a: Usually yes for baking and for anything you want crisp, since preheating gets the cavity and the fan up to temperature. Larger ovens such as the Emeril Lagasse take longer to preheat than compact ones, so plan a few extra minutes.

Unplug it, let it cool and remove the tray, rack and crumb tray to wash by hand. Wipe the interior and door with a damp cloth, and avoid abrasive pads on the stainless exterior of models like the Breville and the Ninja Flip.

faq.q: Can these replace a full-size oven?
faq.a: For most daily cooking, they can for one to four people, but not for large roasts or multiple trays at once. A 26 quart model like the Emeril Lagasse comes closest, while the compact ovens are better as a second oven.

finalTake: For cooks who want presets and more control, the Breville BOV900BSS Smart Oven Air Fryer Pro tops this list. For most households the Cuisinart 8-in-1 is the smarter buy, with 1800W of power and eight functions at a lower price. Choose the Emeril Lagasse for big meals, the Ninja Flip or Our Place for small counters, and the BLACK+DECKER when you want the cheapest way in. Match the oven to your counter and your household, and you will use it every day.
